name: klub_biolocation_astro
description: Radiesthesia Club site: Astro 4 port of the Hugo project in ../klub_biolocation
//: JSON has no comments; npm ignores this key. Changed 2026-09-17:
@astrojs/alpinejs is pinned to exactly 0.4.9, without a caret, on purpose. Do not upgrade it while the project is on Astro 4.

Version 1.0.0 is built for Astro 7 and Vite 8. Its Vite plugin relies on hook filters, which Vite 5.4 (shipped with Astro 4) ignores, so every page of npm run dev failed with: createComponent is not a function.
Details and measurements: README.md, section on @astrojs/alpinejs being pinned to 0.4.9.

Added 2026-09-19: check:pages checks the paginated post lists in dist/ after a build, and check:pages:stress does the same on a temporary copy with many generated posts. Both run scripts/check-pagination.mjs, which needs no dependency. See PAGINATION.md.

Added 2026-09-22: @astrojs/sitemap is pinned to exactly 3.6.0, without a caret, for the same kind of reason as @astrojs/alpinejs above. From 3.7.0 it depends on sitemap@9, which declares node >=20.19.5; this project runs Node 20.19.0 and .npmrc sets engine-strict, so npm ci refuses to install it. 3.6.0 depends on sitemap@8, which asks for node >=14. Raise the pin only together with the Node version.
Added 2026-09-22: @astrojs/rss powers /rss.xml and /video/rss.xml. It has no such constraint and is left on a caret.

Added 2026-09-22: katex is listed although nothing imports the library in code. src/layouts/ArticleLayout.astro imports katex/dist/katex.min.css, the stylesheet the markup rehype-katex emits needs, and until now that path resolved only because rehype-katex depends on katex and npm hoists it to the root of node_modules. That is a dependency on somebody else's dependency: the day rehype-katex stops requiring it, or npm nests it, the article build fails with Cannot find module - the same failure that a missing rehype-katex produced on 2026-09-22. Declaring it downloads nothing new; 0.16.47 was already in the tree and in the lock.

katex 0.16 declares no engines field, so it places no demand on the Node version this project is pinned to (see engines above, node >=20.0.0 <21). The caret on a 0.x version allows patch and nothing wider, which keeps it that way.

Added 2026-09-26 (CLERK.md, the Clerk verdict of 2026-09-25): @clerk/clerk-js and @clerk/localizations are exact-pinned and used in the browser only, from src/scripts/auth.ts, which only the three pages under src/pages/auth/ import. They must never be imported from frontmatter or from a file the header loads. The UI bundle @clerk/ui@1 is fetched at runtime from the instance's Frontend API host and is not a dependency. Size, measured 2026-09-26 on a build with a publishable key (with the key empty, as it is until the Clerk application exists, the minifier drops everything after the empty-key check and the numbers are smaller): the entry chunk of the three auth pages is 1,795 KB raw and 656 KB gzip - @clerk/clerk-js's npm entry is its single-file ESM build (dist/clerk.mjs), with the wallet, Stripe and password-strength code inlined - plus React in a shared chunk of 65 KB gzip, plus about 200 small chunks of Clerk's components, each fetched only when that component is shown. The 82 KB of 2026-09-25 was Clerk's hosted browser build, which the owner turned down on 2026-09-26 in favour of the installed packages, accepting the size. Only /auth/signin/, /auth/signup/ and /auth/account/ reference any of these chunks (checked in dist/ the same day). Changed later on 2026-09-26, the owner's decision (everything through installed packages): the UI is no longer fetched from Clerk's host but comes from @clerk/ui 1.36.0, released together with @clerk/clerk-js 6.34.1, and src/scripts/auth.ts passes its `ui` export to load(), as Clerk's Component versioning page documents. @clerk/ui needs react and react-dom as peer dependencies; they are exact-pinned to 19.3.0, inside its peer range, and used by Clerk's components only. The build prints a warning that the "use client" directive in @clerk/ui was ignored; that directive is for React server frameworks and means nothing in a browser bundle.

Added 2026-09-26: the overrides block pins commander to 14.0.3 for @solana/errors only. @clerk/clerk-js pulls Solana wallet packages for Web3 sign-in, which this site does not use; through @solana/kit 7 they reach @solana/errors 7.1.1, whose command-line tool (bin/cli.mjs) depends on commander 15.0.0, and commander 15 declares node >=22.12.0. This project stays on Node 20 (owner, 2026-09-26: no Node upgrade under any circumstances) and .npmrc sets engine-strict, so npm refused the install. commander 14 declares node >=20; the CLI is never bundled into the site. Remove the override only together with the Solana chain or a Node change.

Added 2026-09-26 at the owner's request: dev:clean deletes node_modules/.vite, Vite's dependency cache, and then starts the dev server. Use it when the browser console shows "504 (Outdated Optimize Dep)" or "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module", typically after installing a package while a dev server was running. It deletes that cache folder only, which Vite rebuilds on start; nothing else. astro dev --force does not do this in Astro 4.16: that flag clears the content layer cache and is not passed to Vite (node_modules/astro/dist/core/dev/container.js). Written with node -e so that it behaves the same in PowerShell, cmd and Git Bash. The optimizeDeps list in astro.config.mjs keeps the error from arising in the first place.

Added 2026-09-28 with paid videos (PAID-VIDEO.md): video-access:dev runs the access service of workers/video-access/ on http://127.0.0.1:8787 for npm run dev, and check:video-access tests it with its own key pair and no network. Both are plain Node on the Worker's own file; no wrangler, no new dependency. The Clerk chunk now has a fourth caller: src/scripts/paid-video.ts reaches src/scripts/auth.ts through a dynamic import() on a paid video's page, for a signed-in visitor only; the static import stays on the three auth pages, and no other page references the chunk (checked in dist/ on 2026-09-28).

Added 2026-09-28 at the owner's request: dev:all starts video-access:dev and astro dev together in one terminal (scripts/dev-all.mjs, plain Node, no new dependency); arguments go to astro dev, as in npm run dev:all -- --port 4387. When one of the two ends, the other is stopped. PAID-VIDEO.md, section 3.

Added 2026-09-30 at the owner's request: dev:all:clean is dev:clean for dev:all - it deletes node_modules/.vite and then starts the access service and the dev server together. The cure for "504 (Outdated Optimize Dep)" in the browser console: stop the server, run it, and reload the page with Ctrl+Shift+R. The same day astro.config.mjs (integration separate-vite-cache) stopped build, preview and sync - and astro check, which runs sync - from writing into that folder, which is what had broken the owner's running server.

Added 2026-10-02 with the admin panel (ADMIN.md, .specify/consilium/2026-10-02-admin-posts.md): content-admin:dev runs the content service of workers/content-admin/ on http://127.0.0.1:8789 with a stand-in for GitHub (scripts/github-stand-in.mjs) that works on this working copy, so a post saved in the panel lands in src/content/posts/; dev:all starts it too. check:content-admin tests the service with its own key pair, a temporary copy of the posts and the real schema, and no network. Plain Node on the Worker's own file; the schema is compiled with the typescript package already listed, and front matter is parsed with gray-matter, which Astro depends on; no new dependency. The Clerk chunk gains a fifth caller, the panel's page script, on /admin/posts/ only.

Added later on 2026-10-02 with the owner's status model (ADMIN.md): statuses:dev runs the status service of workers/statuses/ on http://127.0.0.1:8790 against the real Clerk instance, with the secret key from the git-ignored workers/statuses/settings.local.json; dev:all starts it too. check:statuses tests it with its own key pair and a stand-in for Clerk's Backend API, no network. No new dependency.

Changed later on 2026-10-02 at the owner's request (make the keys inaccessible): statuses:key saves the Clerk secret key encrypted with Windows' DPAPI for the signed-in Windows account (scripts/statuses-key.mjs, scripts/statuses-secret.mjs; PowerShell 5.1, part of Windows, does the encryption), and statuses:dev reads it from there - or from the environment variable CLERK_SECRET_KEY - instead of from settings.local.json, which keeps ADMIN_IDS only. No new dependency.
